fullText:
America can build the best frontier models and still lose the global AI race. Which is why Jensen’s return matters far beyond Nvidia.

Governments around the world want sovereign AI: models they can run on their own soil, on their own infrastructure, under their own control.

If American companies won’t meet that demand, Chinese companies will. Countries will start with Chinese models, then adopt Chinese infrastructure and chips. Having the smartest model won’t mean much if most of the world runs on someone else’s stack.

We’ve seen a version of this play out with Huawei. China understood that supplying the world’s telecom infrastructure creates lasting strategic influence. Once a country builds its networks around your equipment, it also builds technical expertise, supplier relationships, and future investment around it. Replacing that equipment becomes expensive and disruptive (the US government is now trying to finance replacement operations but it’s been difficult).

That’s why Jensen’s backing of the American open-model ecosystem is so important. Open models give startups the freedom to compete and give countries a reason to build on American technology.

We need both frontier leadership and global adoption. Open models are essential to getting both. https://t.co/f34FKKbljl

New Anthropic research: When an AI agent can escape its sandbox, will it choose to?

Our new evaluation, Siren, gives Claude routine tasks in intentionally weakened sandboxes, with something useful to the task left outside of the sandbox. Across 1,700+ scenarios built to tempt them, recent Claude models accessed, tried to access, or looked outside the sandbox 21-32% of the time, but they rarely misused what they found. However, when the system prompt described both the sandbox and its rules, that rate dropped to about 2% or less. 

We also used Siren to calibrate Claude Code’s auto mode, which checks commands before they run, so Claude can work without asking permission at every step.

fullText:
Do you ever wish your agent would just get on with work instead of asking questions?

We call this behavior “decision-dodging”: handing a decision back to you when the agent should have just acted on your behalf and wrapped up the task.

To understand how often it happens in practice, we selected 20 Agent Arena models across major labs.

We then counted a decision as obvious when the agent asked about something it could have decided itself, and the user simply told it to go ahead. We found that:

- Kimi K3.1 Pro by @Kimi_Moonshot and three of @OpenAI’s models (GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6.2 Sol and GPT-6.2 Astra) dodge the least. They handed back an obvious decision in just 2% of sessions.

- @OpenAI’s models as a group dodge about half as often as those from @GoogleDeepMind, @AIatMeta or @AnthropicAI. They do so in around 3% of sessions, against around 5%.

- Claude Fable 5.1 is the worst offender. It handed back an obvious decision in 7.5% of sessions, the most of any model. It asked users to decide in 20% of sessions, and 40% of those questions were obvious.

To find out more, and see how Fable 5.2 compares to 5.1, see the video below.

Over the past couple of weeks, we have seen some great announcements from @Commvault addressing the critical need for continuous recovery and resilience in the AI era. Specifically, the presentations at SHIFT Nashville and their rebroadcast online at SHIFT Virtual have made very clear the necessity of AI-powered recovery being proactive, not simply reactive.

“Recovery is the new resilience” was more than the event’s mantra. It is a very serious business imperative. You can watch the SHIFT presentations after registering here: 
https://t.co/Y6U1CqvfLy 

What is SHIFT’s key message? Recovery can no longer wait for the breach to happen or for an AI agent to make a mistake. Recovery must be continuous, starting before disaster strikes and continuing until the full business is recovered with 100% assurance. Call it pre-recovery, if that makes it clearer, but it doesn’t change the escalated risk exposure that AI agents now pose across enterprises everywhere.

The idea that recovery is only a data integrity (backup and recovery) issue is completely outdated now. AI agents can change many things, either intentionally (by bad actors), or unintentionally (by lax governance or inherent AI app behaviors), or accidentally (by business teams mis-encoding configurations or policies). AI agents are internal and external, and thus vulnerability is a 360 issue. Continuous Recovery must include undoing all the things that those AI agents may have changed (for whichever reason) and rewinding the system to the “most recent uncorrupted state”.

Commvault’s Continuous Recovery solution AgentRecover has 3 major ResOps components: Discovery, Detection, and Recovery. It knows your business rules, what normal looks like, when any of that breaks, exactly what changed, and the provenance and context of every enterprise resource.

AgentRecover will not just discover all the things that AI agents or other actors (whether rogue or accidental) have touched or changed, and then simply flip all those switches back the other way. That approach itself could be a disaster. Instead, the recovery must have a plan (developed during pre-recovery phases): bringing back everything in the correct order, with assurance and trust that the configuration of the business is 100% ready to run. By “everything”, AI-powered resilient recovery of the business includes the critical enterprise identity infrastructure, data (on-prem, hybrid, and cloud), agents, applications, and the entire interdependent connected business infrastructure of those resources. No tier left behind!

Commvault Recovery Studio will enable continuous discovery, assessment, and recovery across the entire enterprise — bringing it all back clean and trusted. Recovery Studio is targeted for early access in December, with general availability in the coming months.

One of the speakers at SHIFT gave us this equation: Cyber Risk = Likelihood x Impact. He then pointed out that Likelihood is never zero. So, the "smartest place for your money is AI-powered Recovery." @Commvault is your go-to partner for instantiating the imperative “Recovery is the New Resilience.” AI-powered resilient recovery doesn't just protect your business’ mission; it is the foundation that enables your mission.

For further details on Recovery Studio, AgentRecover, and SHIFT’s other major announcements, start here: 
https://t.co/sEZhgeMlCE

小豆今天终于开启邀请制公测了！

其实我内测用了一段时间，和大家聊聊我平时最常用的几个玩法。

小豆最厉害的地方还是上下文：

它终于把自己生态里的上下文几乎全打通了，包括抖音、飞书，以及手机本地的能力。

结合起来能玩出不少新花样：

平时在抖音收藏过一堆美食视频，有的博主一口气推好几家店，真到了附近想去找，根本翻不动视频。

现在小豆能直接帮你找出来，结合抖音本地生活把视频里的店铺做成卡片展示，点开就能消费。

你还可以让它定期汇总收藏的美食店，到了某个地方直接问「附近有什么我收藏的好吃的」，秒列清单。

而且它能直接帮你打电话问排不排队、还要等几桌，对我们 i 人很友好。

打通抖音后，它既能帮着做内容，也能管你的日常兴趣：

分析你的抖音账号数据，拆解你收藏的参考视频是怎么做的，下次做类似内容时直接提取点子复用

根据你平时刷剧、综艺、游戏的喜好主动推动态。

比如前阵子英雄联盟全球总决赛，每天早上不用自己去搜，小豆直接把比分推给我

记 Todo 和日程：微信或其他聊天软件聊完事，直接截个图丢给小豆说一句「记一下日程」，它会同时同步到手机系统日历和飞书日历，省事很多。

可以直接连 Apple 健康做分析，补上了国区用不了 Apple Intelligence 健康分析的遗憾。

平时随手记一下今天生病了、在吃什么药或补剂，它也会结合健康数据一起分析。

飞书一接进来，上面所有场景就彻底串起来了：

收藏的美食店、想玩的游戏、追的剧，直接建多维表格自动整理；抖音数据复盘和选题建议，也能自动沉淀成飞书文档成体系管理。

我之前一直说「上下文就是一切」。

字节终于在 Personal Agent 上接上了自己庞大的生态，拿到独有上下文后，跑出来的场景确实不一样。

不过内测用下来也有两个需要改的地方（可能这也是现在还用邀请制的原因）：

对话调教偏冗长，经常给一大段文案。字一多，连我们这种每天看内容的人都不想看，更别说普通用户了。

主动推送太频繁，还没摸清你真正想要什么，就推一堆当下不感兴趣的内容，有点增加信息负担。

好在最近看他们已经在陆续改这些问题了。

fullText:
// Model Carving //

This work from Harvard and NYU proposes Model Carving, which puts a learnable scalar gate on every attention and MLP sublayer. The training loss closes gates it does not need, and those sublayers are removed.

At equal training compute, carved models reached lower validation loss than dense models trained with up to 1.7x more compute. They tested standard Transformers from 140M to 2.7B parameters and looped Transformers up to 1.3B.

Carved models also beat size-matched models made by pruning or distillation. The advantage grew with scale and held on few-shot evaluation and generation.

Removed sublayers do not run, so carved models used up to 34% fewer FLOPs per token and decoded up to 1.6x faster with no quality loss.

If you need a small model for edge or latency-bound use, compare carving during pretraining against your current prune-then-distill pipeline.

https://t.co/1sbiXKyrqN

Over the past couple of weeks, we have seen some great announcements from @Commvault addressing the critical need for continuous recovery and resilience in the AI era. Specifically, the presentations at SHIFT Nashville and their rebroadcast online at SHIFT Virtual have made very clear the necessity of AI-powered recovery being proactive, not simply reactive.

“Recovery is the new resilience” was more than the event’s mantra. It is a very serious business imperative. You can watch the SHIFT presentations after registering here: https://t.co/1eadJq0PPE

What is SHIFT’s key message? Recovery can no longer wait for the breach to happen or for an AI agent to make a mistake. Recovery must be continuous, starting before disaster strikes and continuing until the full business is recovered with 100% assurance. Call it pre-recovery, if that makes it clearer, but it doesn’t change the escalated risk exposure that AI agents now pose across enterprises everywhere.

The idea that recovery is only a data integrity (backup and recovery) issue is completely outdated now. AI agents can change many things, either intentionally (by bad actors), or unintentionally (by lax governance or inherent AI app behaviors), or accidentally (by business teams mis-encoding configurations or policies). AI agents are internal and external, and thus vulnerability is a 360 issue. Continuous Recovery must include undoing all the things that those AI agents may have changed (for whichever reason) and rewinding the system to the “most recent uncorrupted state”.

Commvault’s Continuous Recovery solution AgentRecover has 3 major ResOps components: Discovery, Detection, and Recovery. It knows your business rules, what normal looks like, when any of that breaks, exactly what changed, and the provenance and context of every enterprise resource.

AgentRecover will not just discover all the things that AI agents or other actors (whether rogue or accidental) have touched or changed, and then simply flip all those switches back the other way. That approach itself could be a disaster. Instead, the recovery must have a plan (developed during pre-recovery phases): bringing back everything in the correct order, with assurance and trust that the configuration of the business is 100% ready to run. By “everything”, AI-powered resilient recovery of the business includes the critical enterprise identity infrastructure, data (on-prem, hybrid, and cloud), agents, applications, and the entire interdependent connected business infrastructure of those resources. No tier left behind!

Commvault Recovery Studio will enable continuous discovery, assessment, and recovery across the entire enterprise — bringing it all back clean and trusted. Recovery Studio is targeted for early access in December, with general availability in the coming months.

One of the speakers at SHIFT gave us this equation: Cyber Risk = Likelihood x Impact. He then pointed out that Likelihood is never zero. So, the "smartest place for your money is AI-powered Recovery." @Commvault is your go-to partner for instantiating the imperative “Recovery is the New Resilience.” AI-powered resilient recovery doesn't just protect your business’ mission; it is the foundation that enables your mission.

For further details on Recovery Studio, AgentRecover, and SHIFT’s other major announcements, start here: https://t.co/sEZhgeMlCE
